newsitem.title: UK: Mobil, Amoco mull U.S. downstream link - report.
newsitem.headline: Mobil, Amoco mull U.S. downstream link - report.

text.p: A British newspaper report on Sunday said oil companies Mobil Corp. and Amoco Corp. are discussing a possible merger of their downstream businesses in the United States and overseas.
The Sunday Telegraph said talks had been underway for some months over the merger, given a value of around $20 billion.
It said any pssible merger would not include Europe, where Mobil linked up with BP last year to pool assets worth some $5 billion.
Mobil's Chief Executive Lucio Noto told reporters earlier this month after the company's annual meeting that all companies involved in refining and marketing were looking at joint ventures.
Mobil has a 7 percent to 8 percent share of U.S. oil marketing, but that is heavily concentrated in key regional markets.

In March, Shell Oil Co and Texaco agreed to combine the major elements of their U.S. refining and marketing activities in the Midwest and West, along with transportation, trading and lubricants businesses.
